headerBody: A clear, calm field guide to staying safe, confident and independent abroad — written for the traveler over 60. Nineteen chapters, one scam category each, from airport porters and fake hotel calls to the grandparent-emergency scam — each with ready-to-use refusal scripts and red-flag checklists.
quadHead: The approaches that target older travelers most.

quad.title: Airport Black-Taxi Switch
quad.tl: A ¥120–180 ride to your hotel ticks up to ¥600 — “night rate, traffic surcharge, special road.”

quad.title: The Nanjing-Road Tea House
quad.tl: Four small cups in a 12-seat room — then a ¥3,000–10,000 bill for two. Your new friend vanishes.

quad.title: The Fake Monk’s Bracelet
quad.tl: A robed “monk” near Sensoji slips a gold bracelet onto your wrist as a “gift,” then opens a donation book for ¥3,000–¥10,000. Real monks don’t solicit on the street.

quad.title: The Scippatori Moped Snatch
quad.tl: A two-rider Vespa accelerates past on Via Toledo and the passenger tears the bag or watch off you in one motion — one British tourist lost a €35,000 Rolex from his wrist in broad daylight.

body: Travel Scams for Seniors is a clear, calm field guide to staying safe, confident and independent abroad — written for the traveler over 60 who has no intention of staying home.

Nineteen chapters, one scam category each — airport porters, fake hotel front-desk calls, taxi overcharges, the grandparent-emergency call — each with the exact approach, the red flags, and a word-for-word refusal script you can keep in your pocket.
Re-researched and updated every year — when a new edition ships, it appears in your Kindle library. Written to give you confidence, not fear.
